skill.name: error-memory
skill.description: Records AI assistant mistakes, root causes, and reusable fixes in a project error log.
skill.summary: Maintain a concise project error log for failed builds, missed conventions, and misunderstood requirements.
skill.author: Aceek

security_audit.summary: All eight static findings are false positives from markdown inline code or fenced examples, not real shell execution or reconnaissance. The only semantic issue found is low-risk filesystem persistence: the skill asks the agent to create or append `.claude/errors.md`. No evidence found of prompt injection, network access, credential access, or malicious intent.

remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before creating or modifying `.claude/errors.md` in a repository.
Instruct agents to summarize errors without credentials, private user data, or proprietary details.
Clarify that inline labels and fenced examples are documentation, not executable shell commands.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Project File Modification
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs agents to append to `.claude/errors.md` and create that file when missing. This changes project files and may store sensitive correction details if used without care.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 33-39 explicitly instruct appending to and creating a project file. The behavior is benign but still affects the filesystem.

content.value_statement: AI coding assistants can repeat mistakes after failed builds, missed conventions, or user corrections. This skill creates a concise project error memory with causes and reusable rules.
actual_capabilities: Prompts the agent to record build or test failures after its actions.
Classifies mistakes as technical, context, or comprehension errors.
Guides root cause analysis before writing a reusable fix rule.
Provides a starter template and legend for a missing error file.
Encourages checking past errors before acting on a project.
limitations: Does not run tests, builds, or validation commands.
Relies on the agent or user to decide when an error occurred.
Stores notes in project files, so sensitive details need care.
Does not synchronize error memory across separate projects.

use_cases.title: Recover After Failed Builds
use_cases.description: Record why a build failed and define a rule that prevents repeating the same technical mistake.

use_cases.title: Preserve Project Conventions
use_cases.description: Capture missed patterns or repository conventions after a correction, so future edits follow local expectations.

use_cases.title: Improve Assistant Follow-Up
use_cases.description: Turn user corrections into short project memory entries that guide later assistant decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Record a Simple Mistake
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner use after a clear error.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use error-memory to record the mistake from this failed test. Classify it, name the root cause, and add one reusable rule.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Missed Convention
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after the user corrects a repository pattern.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use error-memory for this convention correction. Explain what I missed, why it happened, and the rule I should follow next time.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Multiple Failures
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after several related build or test errors.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the recent failures and use error-memory to add concise entries for each distinct root cause. Avoid duplicate symptoms.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Before Continuing
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced use before risky follow-up work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Before making the next change, check the project error memory and apply any relevant rules to this task.

output_examples.input: The assistant used the wrong test command and broke the local validation flow.
output_examples.output: A short technical error entry records the wrong command, the missed project convention, and the correct validation rule.

output_examples.input: The user corrected an implementation that ignored an existing project pattern.
output_examples.output: A context error entry explains the missed pattern and adds a future rule to inspect neighboring files first.

output_examples.input: The assistant misunderstood a request and changed unrelated behavior.
output_examples.output: A comprehension error entry notes the misunderstanding and creates a rule to confirm scope before editing.

best_practices: Ask before creating or changing the project error file.
Write one short entry per distinct root cause.
Remove secrets, private data, and unnecessary blame from entries.
anti_patterns: Do not record long narratives that hide the reusable rule.
Do not store credentials, private messages, or sensitive business context.
Do not treat symptoms as root causes.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps an AI assistant remember project mistakes, root causes, and rules that prevent repeated errors.

faq.question: Where does it store the error memory?
faq.answer: The skill instructs the assistant to use `.claude/errors.md` in the project when the user allows it.

faq.question: Does it run commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill only describes a documentation workflow and does not include executable scripts.

faq.question: Can it replace tests or code review?
faq.answer: No. It records lessons from mistakes, but tests and review still verify code quality.

faq.question: Is it useful for teams?
faq.answer: Yes. Teams can use it to preserve common conventions and prevent repeated assistant errors.

faq.question: What should be excluded from entries?
faq.answer: Exclude secrets, private user details, proprietary context, and anything not needed for the future rule.
